Every payment you make onchain is a public receipt: your salary, your rent, what you spent last night. All of it sitting on a block explorer forever, readable by anyone who bothers to look.

Sealed is a private money account on Starknet built to stop that.

Most "private" crypto tools shield one step: a transfer, a mixer hop. Then you spend from a normal wallet and the trail reconnects on the other side.

Sealed shields the loop instead.

Shielded balances. A card that spends straight from them. A fresh funding identity per transaction.

And spend rules you program, so one swipe both pays the merchant and moves money where you told it to.

One carve-out, stated plainly: the card's settlement leg runs through a hosted account we operate. That account is custodial and we label it as such in the app, rather than implying the whole loop is trustless.

An actual transaction, not a mockup. A Sealed account sells private STRK and pays a merchant in USDC in a single call:

Every merchant sees a fresh identity, not your main account. Each spend is funded through a freshly derived onchain identity, so one payment's funding leg doesn't link to the next.

The honest caveat on that: settlement itself still lands on a fixed program address today. Per-merchant settlement addressing is the next piece, not something we're claiming now.

Funding bridges in from another chain. We moved USDC from Base: it mints on Starknet, then shields into the pool in the very next transaction. The mint is briefly visible, the shield is not.

0x28b053d9a670650604bf8f7ae8b67fc7f296d2f4fa630a987e7a6f775b11fe2

The card is the part people don't believe until they see the decisioning logs. We ran it against Lithic's Authorization Stream API, a real issuer sandbox: an over-limit swipe declined, an in-policy grocery swipe approved. Both recorded on Lithic's side.
You program what a swipe does. Set a rule, and every restaurant purchase lends 10 STRK into the Earn vault in the same transaction that pays the merchant. No second signature, no separate trip.

To be exact about that vault: it is our own ERC-4626 contract, 1:1. Deposit STRK, mint the same number of shares, redeem to get it back.

It's a lockbox, not a yield strategy. There is no rate to quote and we don't quote one.

When someone needs proof a payment happened, you don't hand over your whole history. A viewing key generates a statement for that one authorization: proves it happened, exposes nothing else in the account.

Where this actually stands: everything above runs on Starknet Sepolia, real transactions, test money. The card is Lithic's sandbox, not a live program.

We say so because a privacy product that hides its own stage isn't one you should trust.

What is on mainnet: we shielded real STRK into the canonical STRK20 privacy pool, and those transactions are Accepted on L1, settled on Ethereum rather than just sequenced.

Two of our contract classes are declared there too. Declared isn't deployed.

We sent work back upstream as well: a PR and an issue against StarkWare's own privacy SDK, plus a public starter repo if you want to build a shielded account yourself.
